successors.text: Seleucia, the small principality of Vologases VI: he 'continued to rule Seleucia until 221/2' (Vologases VI page); 'would rule a small principality centered around Seleucia until 221/2' (Artabanus IV…

ledger.x: c. 213: Artabanus IV rebels and Vologases VI is left holding Seleucia. Vologases VI page: 'uncontested king of the Parthian Empire from 208 to 213'; his brother's rebellion 'most likely started in c. 213'; Vologases 'kept Seleucia, where he minted coins'. The state is entered from the year the civil war begins; the…

c. 213: the brothers' war begins and Artabanus IV overruns Media and Susa. Artabanus IV page: 'The dynastic struggle between the two brothers most likely started about 213'; 'Artabanus successfully conquered much of the empire, including Media and Susa'. The counterpart is the Parthian Empire as ruled by Artabanus IV.
By 216: Artabanus IV holds most of the empire and Rome recognises him as supreme ruler.
221/2: Vologases VI's principality at Seleucia ends.

wars.name: Parthian civil war of Artabanus IV and Vologases VI
wars.outcome: Artabanus IV held most of the empire from 216, with Roman recognition, while Vologases VI kept Seleucia until 221/2; Artabanus was defeated and killed by Ardashir I on 28 April 224.

certainty.note: No boundary on either page; the Seleucia enclave is a disc, drawn to 222 (the end of his rule of Seleucia on both pages).
